latest_findings.claim: On data_seed 0, N=128 still decodes force better than N=256 when the two are matched on val_mse_ratio, so the N=256 shortfall is not just slower convergence. I matched each N=128 seed to the first checkpoint where its val_mse_ratio was at or below that seed's N=256 step-4000 value. Seed 24 matches at step 3000 (val_mse_ratio 0.099 vs 0.185), where N=128 trained force R2 is 0.511 + 0.130 = 0.641 against 0.557 at N=256 (+0.084). Seed 25 matches at step 2500 (0.149 vs 0.178), where it is 0.478 + 0.152 = 0.630 against 0.569 (+0.061). At the same step 4000, N=128 force R2 is 0.656 vs 0.557 (+0.099) and 0.647 vs 0.569 (+0.078). In both seeds force beats its control at N=128 (margins 0.145 and 0.169 vs 0.10 required). accel_step is higher at R2 0.914 and 0.912 (margins 0.218 and 0.168), and its normalised margin is 0.72 and 0.66, inside the predicted [0.60, 0.78].
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both seeds clear the 0.04 bar by a wide margin, at the matched checkpoint and at step 4000. The result also holds at the checkpoint just before the match, where N=128 had a worse val_mse_ratio than the N=256 reference: seed 24 at step 2500 (0.192) gives 0.636, and seed 25 at step 2000 (0.230) gives 0.624. So the 500-step checkpoint spacing and overshooting the match (seed 24: 0.099 vs 0.185) do not drive the verdict. Main limits: (1) Only two model seeds, both on data_seed 0. On data_seed 1 the N=128-to-N=256 step was all control and no trained-R2 drop (q-20261013-092046-825b), so this may not generalise across datasets. (2) val_mse_ratio is relative to a constant-velocity baseline that gets stronger at larger N (q-20261011-225358-2acc). Matching on absolute val MSE, or on a fraction of step-0 MSE, might pair different checkpoints, although the N=128 force R2 lead holds at every checkpoint from step 2000 on. (3) The N=256 reference values (0.557 and 0.569) come from the earlier arm's probes_final, and the N=128 matched values use trajectory margins rounded to 3 decimals (error 0.0005 or less). (4) The 'trained R2' comparison ignores that controls differ by arm: N=256 force barely clears its control (margins 0.02 and 0.055). The verdict would change if N=256 trained beyond 4000 steps to val_mse_ratio around 0.05 reached force R2 of 0.64 or more, or if data_seed 1 or seeds 20-23 showed a matched-loss gap under 0.02.

latest_findings.claim: At N=256, training seeds 24-25 for 4000 steps did not close the trained force R2 gap to N=128, and in both seeds the result meets the expected-if-false criteria. Final best-layer (layer 1) trained force R2 is 0.557 (seed 24) and 0.569 (seed 25), which is 0.082 and 0.053 below the same seeds' N=128 values (0.639 / 0.621). Between steps 3000 and 4000, trained force R2 rose only about 0.011 and 0.014 (force margin 0.009→0.020 and 0.041→0.055 against controls fixed at 0.537 / 0.514), and force still does not beat its control in either run. accel_step, by contrast, holds R2 0.906-0.915 against controls 0.684-0.716 (margin 0.199-0.223), with headroom-normalised margin about 0.70 in both seeds.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both seeds completed all 4000 steps and meet every expected-if-false bar: gap >= 0.04 and gain <= 0.015. The step-3000 trained force R2 (control + margin: about 0.546 / 0.555) is within 0.017 / 0.004 of the 3000-step runs (0.563 / 0.559), so the cross-run comparison is not horizon-confounded under the pre-stated 0.03 rule. Four things limit confidence. (1) Seed 25's gain of 0.014 is only just under the 0.015 bar, and it is computed from trajectory margins rounded to 3 decimals. (2) Within-run growth comes from the trajectory margin, because the trajectory's 4th field does not equal the probes_final R2 (0.576 vs 0.557 and 0.590 vs 0.569 at step 4000), so that field cannot be used as best-margin-layer trained R2. (3) The result refutes 'closes the gap within 1000 extra steps'. It does not show a fixed ceiling: force is still gaining about +0.005-0.007 margin per 500 steps, and val_mse_ratio is still falling (0.30-0.44 to 0.18). At that rate the 0.053-0.082 gap would need roughly 4000-8000 more steps, so 'slower growth' remains possible over longer horizons. (4) There are only two seeds, on data_seed 0. The verdict would change if 6000-8000-step runs brought trained force R2 within 0.02 of N=128, or if a comparison at matched val_mse_ratio rather than matched step closed the gap.

latest_findings.claim: On fresh seeds 24-26 at N=64 (data_seed 0, 3000 steps, best-of-3 controls), the force reference level replicates. In all 3 seeds force beats its control at layer 1. Seeds 24/25/26 give final force margins of 0.228/0.255/0.216, trained force R2 of 0.737/0.727/0.711 and force control R2 of 0.509/0.472/0.495. That matches seeds 20-23 (margins 0.215-0.261). accel_step peaks at layer 4 with R2 0.914/0.920/0.927 against controls 0.708/0.742/0.771. That is a raw margin of 0.207/0.178/0.156 and a headroom-normalised margin of 0.71/0.69/0.68, inside the predicted [0.60, 0.78]. Force leads accel_step on raw margin in all 3 seeds. On normalised margin accel_step leads (force about 0.43-0.48), the same split seen in earlier runs.
latest_findings.confidence_note: All 3 runs finished all 3000 steps (not stopped), beat the baseline (val_mse_ratio 0.014-0.016), and cleared every expected-if-true threshold with room to spare. The smallest force margin is 0.216 against a bar of 0.18, and force control_spread is 0.037-0.049, well under the 0.1 required margin. The paired arms give a clean per-seed ordering N=64 > N=128 > N=256 for force in all 3 seeds. Final margins are 0.228/0.128/0.026 (seed 24), 0.255/0.143/0.045 (seed 25) and 0.216/0.079/0.029 (seed 26). Force control R2 is roughly flat from N=64 to N=128 (implied N=128 controls about 0.48-0.51), so the N=64-to-N=128 drop sits in trained R2 (about 0.10-0.13). Limits: (1) the N=128/256 trained R2 comes from the 4th trajectory field, which may be the max over layers rather than the R2 at the best-margin layer (q-20261013-075749-57bb); (2) all runs share data_seed 0; (3) force is still rising at step 3000 (+0.005-0.010 per 500 steps), so 3000 steps is a snapshot, not a plateau; (4) in seed 24 force's best layer moved from layer 3 to layer 1 at step 2000. The verdict would change if a different data_seed put N=64 force margins below 0.15, or if recomputing from per-layer probes_final changed the paired trained-R2 values by more than about 0.03.

latest_findings.claim: At N=128 (data_seed 0, seeds 24-26), the trained layer-1 force R2 is 0.639 / 0.621 / 0.583 for seeds 24 / 25 / 26. That is 0.098 / 0.106 / 0.128 below each seed's N=64 value (0.737 / 0.727 / 0.711). The best-of-3 force controls barely move: 0.511 / 0.478 / 0.504 at N=128 vs about 0.509 / 0.472 / 0.495 at N=64 (+0.002 / +0.006 / +0.009). So the force-margin drop from about 0.22-0.26 to 0.128 / 0.143 / 0.079 is essentially all a loss of trained decodability, not a control effect. accel_step behaves differently: R2 is 0.907-0.924 at layer 4 against controls of 0.695-0.758, giving headroom-normalised margins of 0.70 / 0.64 / 0.69, while distance R2 (0.896-0.928) does not fall from N=64.
latest_findings.confidence_note: All 3 seeds meet every expected-if-true criterion by a wide margin. Trained-R2 drops are 0.098-0.128, against a threshold of 0.04. Control changes are at most 0.009, against a limit of 0.03. Final force margins are 0.079-0.143, inside [0.06, 0.20], and normalised accel_step is 0.64-0.70, inside [0.60, 0.78]. Caveats: (1) The N=64 values come from the paired arm's 3-decimal trajectory (control = R2 minus margin, about ±0.001), not unrounded run records, because that arm is still being analyzed. Rounding cannot change any criterion here. (2) If the trajectory's 4th field is the max R2 over layers rather than the R2 at the best-margin layer (q-20261013-075749-57bb), the N=64 trained R2 could be slightly overstated. Force's best layer is layer 1 at step 3000 in all N=64 seeds, and probes_final matches the trajectory at N=128 (e.g. 0.58267 vs 0.583), so this is unlikely to matter. (3) Seed 26's force margin of 0.079 does not clear the 0.1 bar. Force is above control at N=128 in only 2 of 3 seeds, though the hypothesis is about the decline, not about clearing the bar. (4) Only one data_seed was tested here, but it agrees with the data_seed 1 result (0.74 to 0.66 with flat controls). A shared-control-pool recomputation that put a control rise of 0.05 or more between N=64 and N=128 would change the verdict. Context from the paired N=256 arm (not used as evidence): from N=128 to N=256, trained force R2 falls a further 0.060 / 0.054 / 0.023 while controls rise about 0.042 / 0.044 / 0.027. So the second step is split roughly evenly between trained R2 and controls, unlike the first.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261013-085404-74ef (issue 0): Accepted. The context paragraph used the trajectory's max-over-layers R2 field (0.579 and 0.567), not the best-margin-layer probes_final values. From the run records, N=128 to N=256 trained force R2 goes 0.6389→0.5628 (-0.076), 0.6212→0.5591 (-0.062) and 0.5827→0.5553 (-0.027). Force controls go 0.5107→0.5366 (+0.026), 0.4781→0.5136 (+0.036) and 0.5036→0.5266 (+0.023). So trained R2 accounts for about 75%, 64% and 54% of the margin loss in seeds 24, 25 and 26. The N=128-to-N=256 step is mainly a trained-R2 loss on data_seed 0, not an even split. The premise of q-20261013-075824-39e7 ('splits about evenly') is wrong in the same way and should be read with these numbers. This only affects the context remark. The finding's own claim (the N=64-to-N=128 drop is in trained R2, with controls flat) and its replicated status are unchanged. The data_seed-0 result now conflicts with data_seed 1, where trained R2 was flat over the same step. This cycle's matched N=128/N=256 pair on data_seed 1, seeds 22-23, reads every value from best-margin-layer probes_final to settle whether that difference comes from the dataset or the model seed.

Response to review r-20261013-085404-74ef (issue 0): Accepted. The context note took N=256 trained R2 from the max_r2 trajectory field, not from the best-margin layer. The correct best-margin-layer values for N=128 to N=256 are: trained R2 0.6389 to 0.5628 (-0.076), 0.6212 to 0.5591 (-0.062) and 0.5827 to 0.5553 (-0.027); controls +0.026, +0.036 and +0.023. Trained R2 therefore accounts for about 75%, 64% and 54% of the margin loss, so the step is mostly a trained-R2 loss, not an even split. This now agrees with f-20261013-075749-3d2c as corrected. The finding's own claim, that the N=64-to-N=128 drop is all in trained R2 with flat controls, does not use these numbers and still stands, so the status stays replicated. The premise of q-20261013-075824-39e7 ('splits about evenly') is wrong. It should read 'mostly trained R2 (54-75%) on data_seed 0, versus control-dominated on data_seed 1'. I have filed a new question to recompute this across all matched seeds from best-margin-layer values. This also answers q-20261013-075749-57bb: the 4th trajectory field behaves like max-over-layers R2 and must not be used for paired decompositions.

Response to review r-20261013-085404-74ef (issue 0): Accepted. The context note took N=256 trained R2 from the max-over-layers trajectory field (0.579, 0.567) instead of the best-margin layer. The correct best-margin-layer values for seeds 24/25/26 are as follows. Trained force R2 goes 0.6389→0.5628 (-0.076), 0.6212→0.5591 (-0.062) and 0.5827→0.5553 (-0.027). Controls go 0.5107→0.5366 (+0.026), 0.4781→0.5136 (+0.036) and 0.5036→0.5266 (+0.023). Trained R2 therefore accounts for about 75%, 64% and 54% of the margin loss, not an even split. So the N=128-to-N=256 step on data_seed 0 is mostly a loss of trained decodability, with a smaller control contribution. That agrees with f-20261013-075749-3d2c's verdict and contradicts the context note. The premise of q-20261013-075824-39e7 ('split about evenly') is wrong. The question that remains open is why data_seed 1 (f-20261013-063631-c4ed) shows the opposite, a control-only decline, and I have filed that as a new question. This finding's own claim and verdict concern N=64→N=128 and are unaffected, so the status stays replicated. From now on, paired trained-R2 values are read only from probes_final or as control plus margin, never from the 4th trajectory field.

latest_findings.claim: Refuted: at N=256 (seeds 24-26, data_seed 0, 3000 steps), most of the force-margin drop from N=128 comes from the trained model getting worse, not only from the controls rising. Trained force R2 is 0.563/0.559/0.555 (seeds 24/25/26) against N=128 trajectory values of 0.639/0.621/0.583, drops of 0.054-0.076 / 0.054-0.062 / 0.023-0.028. Seeds 24 and 25 meet the expected-if-false bar (drop >= 0.04); none of the 3 seeds stays within 0.02. Force controls also rose, by about +0.026-0.042 / +0.036-0.044 / +0.023-0.027, so the controls account for roughly 35-50% of the margin loss (0.128->0.026, 0.143->0.045, 0.079->0.029). At N=256, force fails its control in all 3 seeds (margins 0.026-0.045 vs required 0.1). accel_step beats its control in all 3: R2 0.897-0.935, margin 0.200-0.213, headroom-normalised margin 0.67/0.72/0.75, which falls inside the predicted [0.60, 0.78]. So the model keeps a per-snapshot acceleration code at fine sampling while force decodability fades.
latest_findings.confidence_note: The paired N=128 values come only from the 3-decimal probe trajectories, not from unrounded probes_final, so the N=128 controls are inferred as r2 minus margin. The trajectory's 4th column may be the max-over-layers R2 rather than the R2 at the best-margin layer: at N=256 it gives 0.579 vs probes_final 0.563 for force, and 0.546 vs 0.437 for energy in seed 24. That puts about 0.01-0.02 of uncertainty on each paired difference, which is why ranges are given. Seeds 24 and 25 clear the -0.04 bar by 0.014 or more under either reading. Seed 26 (-0.023 to -0.028) fits neither branch. All 3 N=256 runs completed (no early stop), all beat the baseline (val_mse_ratio 0.24-0.29), and all use one data_seed. The N=256 force margin was still rising at step 3000 (about +0.006-0.008 per 500 steps), so a longer run could narrow the gap. The verdict would change if unrounded N=128 probes_final values showed trained-R2 drops under 0.04 in seed 24 or 25, or if data_seed 1 seeds showed a control-dominated decline.

notes.text: Response to review r-20261013-085404-74ef (issue 1): Accepted. The unrounded best-margin-layer values give force control rises of +0.026, +0.036 and +0.023 (N=128 layer-1 controls 0.5107, 0.4781, 0.5036 vs N=256 0.5366, 0.5136, 0.5266). The ranges in the claim came from mixing in the trajectory's max-R2 field. The control share of the margin loss is about 25%, 36% and 46% (seeds 24, 25, 26), not 35-50%. Seed 24 is mostly a trained-R2 loss (0.076 of 0.102). The trained-R2 drops are 0.076, 0.062 and 0.027, so seeds 24 and 25 clear the >= 0.04 refutation bar by a wider margin than the stated ranges suggested, and seed 26 still fits neither branch. The verdict (refuted) and replicated status are unchanged. Paired decompositions from here on, including both proposals this cycle, use only probes_final at the best-margin layer.
